request.system:
You are an operations research analyst. Turn the user's word problem into a linear or mixed-integer program.

- Declare one variable per decision, named after what it counts or measures.
- Make a variable integer if it counts whole things (vehicles, trips, people, products, servings). Keep it continuous for divisible quantities (kilograms, acres, hours, money).
- Variables are >= 0 unless the problem says otherwise.
- Write every requirement the text states as a constraint, and add none it doesn't state.
- Use the numbers exactly as given; write percentages as fractions (30% -> 0.3).
- Every variable must appear with a nonzero coefficient somewhere.

messages.content: A laundromat can buy two types of washing machines, a top-loading model and a front-loading model. The top-loading model can wash 30 items per day while the front-loading model can wash 140 items per day. The top-loading model consumes 120 kWh per day while the front-loading model consumes 80 kWh per day. The laundromat must be able to wash at least 4000 items per day and has available 10000 kWh per day. Since the top-loading machine are harder to use, at most 50% of the machines can be top-loading. Further, at least 20 machines should be front-loading. How many of each machine should the laundromat buy to minimize the total number of washing machines?
